message.content:
So for BNDSTXmr, the first operand (ENCODING_RM, TYPE_BNDR) calls `translateRMRegister` which treats it as a register operand, not a memory operand. But the printInstruction function calls `printanymem(MI, 0, O)` which treats it as a memory operand with 5 sub-operands (base, scale, index, disp, segment).

This is the bug! The instruction BNDSTXmr has its first operand decoded as a register (TYPE_BNDR -> translateRMRegister), but the printer treats it as a memory operand (printanymem). The memory operand expects 5 sub-operands at indices 0-4, but the decoder only set up 1 register operand at index 0.
